name: The Chrome Ceiling: How SNT Created a New Class System
author: Dr. Fatima Okonkwo-Strand, GLMZ Social Studies Institute
body:
Before SNT, the rich and the poor had the same bodies. After SNT, they do not.

SNT made cybernetic augmentation seamless. It made chrome feel like flesh. And by doing so, it created a class divide that is not merely economic or social but biological. The augmented body is objectively more capable than the unaugmented one. It sees better, moves faster, thinks quicker, heals more efficiently. In an economy that rewards capability, the augmented have an insurmountable advantage.

This is the Chrome Ceiling: the invisible barrier that prevents unaugmented individuals from competing with augmented ones for employment, status, and survival.

In the GLMZ labor market:
— 73% of Tier 3+ jobs require or 'strongly prefer' some form of augmentation
— Average income for augmented workers exceeds unaugmented workers by 240%
— Unaugmented applicants receive 60% fewer interview callbacks for augmentation-preferred positions
— The gap is widening. In 2215, the income difference was 180%. In 2220, it was 210%. In 2225, it is 240%.

SNT enabled this divide. Before SNT, cyberware was clumsy, painful, and obviously mechanical. The augmented were visibly different. They could be accommodated, regulated, or excluded. After SNT, the augmented are indistinguishable from the unaugmented until they demonstrate capabilities that flesh cannot match. The discrimination is invisible because the augmentation is invisible.

The most insidious aspect is the normalization. When 62% of the GLMZ population has at least one SNT-bonded implant, the unaugmented are the minority. They are not discriminated against — they are simply left behind. The world accelerates around them. Job requirements escalate. Physical standards rise. Social expectations shift. Nobody is excluding the unaugmented. The unaugmented are just too slow for a world that has been optimized for chrome.
